Share SOC 2/ISO evidence pack and KMS integration guide
Schedule on-site PoC capacity test week of Dec 8
action_items: Daniel Park - prepare VPC diagram with NAT/Egress patterns - 2026-11-25
Omar Khalid - supply list of permitted egress hosts and IP ranges - 2026-11-23
Alicia Gomez - provide pricing for Dedicated vs Private with burstable capacity - 2026-11-24
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-19 | 16:00 PST | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Gomez (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood Solutions), Ravi Menon (CTO - Seabright), Lena Ortiz (Head of Infra), Omar Khalid (Security Engineer), Priya Shah (Compliance)
Summary: deep dive on private/VPC deployment security posture, ingress/egress constraints for regulated trading data, KMS/HSM options, SOC2 artifact requests, RBAC/SSO mapping. Customer concerned about egress and third-party telemetry.
Topics: VPC topology, egress firewall patterns, bastion / jump host approach, private endpoints, KMS integration and HSM vs cloud KMS, audit logging and SIEM ingestion, RBAC and SSO provisioning.

00:00:05 Alicia: ok, good afternoon everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Alicia, AE on the account, with Daniel who will lead the technical bits.
00:00:18 Ravi: hey thanks, we have a pretty tight window to validate architecture for our regulated trading workloads, so want to get into specifics.
00:00:30 Daniel: great, we'll walk through our recommended VPC patterns and then map them to your requirements around data residency and egress control.
00:00:44 Lena: one quick clarifier — when you say private deployment, do you mean a customer-managed control plane in our VPC or a fully on-prem appliance?
00:00:55 Daniel: good question. Redwood Private can run in both modes. for this conversation assume control plane in your VPC with optional on-prem worker nodes. we can support an air-gapped install but that's a separate engagement.
00:01:10 Priya: from a compliance angle we need SOC 2 artifacts, key rotation proof, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. also need SSO/SCIM integration.
00:01:23 Alicia: yes, we'll attach the SOC 2 pack. SCIM + SAML are supported out of the box; Daniel will show how role mappings look.
00:01:35 Daniel: sliding into the topology slide — recommended: management subnet for control plane (private endpoints only), worker subnets in isolated AZs, NAT egress through a centralized egress gateway, and VPC endpoints for S3, Secrets Manager, and private registry.
00:01:50 Omar: when you say egress gateway, is that a NAT gateway, proxy, or firewall appliance? we can't allow direct internet egress from workers.
00:02:03 Daniel: typically customers use a hardened egress proxy (squid or envoy) inside a dedicated subnet with strict ACLs, and then a network firewall for outbound rules. NAT gateway is simpler but has less control for allow-listing FQDNs.
00:02:20 Lena: we need TLS interception for some telemetry to inspect payloads — is that supported?
00:02:28 Daniel: we recommend terminating TLS at the egress proxy for inspection, but we also support MTLS between workers and internal services. note that payload inspection has compliance implications, so coordinate with Priya.
00:02:41 Priya: correct, we need to document our inspection controls for ISO.
00:02:49 Alicia: quick note on KMS — we support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and also can integrate with an HSM via customer HSM or AWS CloudHSM.
00:02:59 Ravi: we prefer HSM-backed keys for model encryption at rest. how does key rotation work?
00:03:08 Daniel: keys can be rotated via KMS policies. for CloudHSM the HSM holds the root key and Redwood stores envelope keys. rotation is supported with asymmetric wrapping to avoid re-encrypting large artifacts.
00:03:22 Omar: are any keys stored in plaintext on instances? we need to avoid key material on disk in readable form.
00:03:30 Daniel: no plaintext. we use in-memory KMS client and envelope encryption; private key handles are ephemeral in the process memory and never persisted. there may be logs referencing key IDs but not material.
00:03:45 00:03:47 Ravi: okay that's good.
00:03:50 Daniel: going back to audit logs — we can stream audit events to your SIEM using an S3 sink with bucket policies and a Kinesis Firehose, or push directly to your Splunk/Datadog via TLS endpoints. logs include request metadata, model version, route, and token-count metrics.
00:04:10 Priya: do logs include PII or full prompts? we need to make sure sensitive prompts are redacted before leaving our environment.
00:04:20 Daniel: excellent point — by default Redwood can be configured with prompt redaction hooks that run as a sidecar before logs are emitted, so you can scrub PII fields. customers often use regex-based filters or a PII detection model.
00:04:36 Lena: what about KV cache or prefix cache spills? any chance cached content ends up in logs?
00:04:44 Daniel: KV cache is in-memory on the worker and never written to persistent logs. we do emit cache hit/miss metrics, but not content. note: transcription sometimes incorrectly reads KV as K-V cash in our exported notes, haha.
00:04:58 Maya: (laughs) I've seen that.
00:05:05 Omar: for our regulated trading path we must enforce egress allow-listing to external exchanges only. can Redwood run dynamic allow-lists?
00:05:16 Daniel: yes, the egress gateway can be updated via an API; you can push CIDR/FQDN updates and we support integration with your IPAM for automated updates.
00:05:27 Ravi: we also need to throttle large model downloads and pin model versions to avoid drift — how do you handle version pinning?
00:05:36 Daniel: customers can pin model versions at route-level. deploys are versioned and support canary rollouts with automatic rollback if latency or quality regressions are detected.
00:05:47 00:06:00 Alicia: quick break — any questions so far?
00:06:03 Priya: SOC 2 — can you share the last audit period and whether Redwood's SOC covers Private installs?
00:06:12 Alicia: Redwood's SOC 2 covers the hosted control plane; for Private we provide a SOC evidence pack and support customers during their own assessment. Private on-prem is usually evaluated as part of the customer's scope.
00:06:26 Priya: ok we'll need a statement that confirms what artifacts Redwood will sign-off on.
00:06:31 Alicia: noted, we'll send a tailored statement.
00:06:36 Lena: network hardening — do you support VPN termination into our VPC and also support for an internal bastion host for operator access?
00:06:46 Daniel: yes, we support IPSec VPNs and private peering. operator access is typically handled via a bastion/jump box with strict RBAC and ephemeral keys — we also recommend integrating with your session manager for audit trails.
00:06:58 Omar: can operators access worker logs directly? we prefer logs to be forwarded to SIEM and access via role-based console only.
00:07:08 Daniel: by default, operators can access logs through the management console with RBAC. for stricter controls you can disable console access and only allow SIEM ingestion; audit events for any console access are emitted.
00:07:24 00:07:30 Ravi: downtime and failover — if egress gateway fails how do workers behave?
00:07:36 Daniel: we recommend multiple egress nodes with health checks and a fail-open vs fail-closed policy determined by you. for regulated workloads most choose fail-closed to prevent any external calls until gateway is healthy.
00:07:50 Lena: fail-closed sounds safer but we need automated alerts to ops. does Redwood emit detailed network health metrics?
00:07:58 Daniel: yes, per-route latency and egress success/failure metrics; we also emit tracer metrics for path diagnostics.
00:08:08 Priya: encryption in transit — is MTLS supported between components?
00:08:13 Daniel: yes, all internal RPCs can be MTLS with customer-provided certs or our managed cert pipeline.
00:08:22 Omar: we need to prove non-repudiation for certain admin actions — do you have immutable audit trails for admin changes?
00:08:31 Daniel: changes to role mappings, key rotations, and deployments are captured in immutable audit logs with change hashes; we can forward those to your archival store for retention.
00:08:42 Alicia: moving on to SSO — Redwood supports SAML and OIDC; SCIM for provisioning. typical mapping is to map your AD groups to Redwood roles (admin, devops, viewer).
00:08:55 Priya: can we enforce MFA for all admin roles?
00:08:59 Daniel: yes, MFA can be enforced at the IdP level and Redwood will respect the assertion. additionally, we support step-up auth for sensitive operations.
00:09:12 Lena: session TTLs? we need short-lived tokens for console sessions and operator commands.
00:09:18 Daniel: session TTLs are configurable; defaults are conservative but you can shorten them down to minutes.
00:09:26 00:09:30 Ravi: about data residency — our trading logs must remain in eu-west-1. how do you ensure model artifacts and logs stay in region?
00:09:38 Daniel: you can pin deployment region and we will ensure S3 buckets, model artifacts, and cache nodes are in that region. cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled by default.
00:09:52 Omar: any dependencies on third-party telemetry that phone-home to Redwood? we block that in our environment.
00:09:59 Daniel: Redwood Private does not phone home telemetry by default. there is an optional telemetry channel for usage statistics which can be disabled. automatic crash reports can be routed to your internal collector.
00:10:10 Alicia: quick note — we also offer a Purpose-built hardened image for on-prem that removes outbound connectors.
00:10:18 Lena: walk me through a sample egress rule set you recommend.
00:10:22 Daniel: rule set example: allow outbound to A) your exchange IP ranges over TLS 443, B) internal token key manager endpoints on port 443, C) container registry private endpoint. deny everything else. for updates to allow-list use API with signed requests.
00:10:40 Priya: what about DNS exfiltration risks — do you support DNS proxying?
00:10:46 Daniel: yes, we recommend forcing DNS through your resolver and using DNS proxying with response policy zones to block exfiltration.
00:10:56 00:11:10 Ravi: let's discuss a concrete deployment scenario — we need model inference for pre-trade risk checks in eu-west-1 with sub-100ms SLO and logs shipped to Splunk in our EU tenancy. can that be done privately?
00:11:23 Daniel: yes, with dedicated worker pools in eu-west-1 you can meet sub-100ms for smaller models; for larger models you'd want a dedicated GPU pool sized to request concurrency. logs can be pushed via Firehose or direct TLS to Splunk with mutual auth.
00:11:40 Lena: how do you ensure determinism in latency when autoscaling kicks in?
00:11:46 Daniel: we pre-warm fixed capacity for burst protection and use a queueing/backpressure mechanism with priority lanes for pre-trade traffic so it doesn't starve.
00:11:58 Omar: from a security perspective, we want to ensure the image supply chain is verified — do you sign images?
00:12:05 Daniel: yes, images and model binaries are signed. you can validate signatures via your artifact verifier and we can provide provenance metadata.
00:12:16 Priya: any certifications for the build pipeline?
00:12:20 Alicia: we maintain secure build practices and can share pipeline attestation documents as part of the SOC pack.
00:12:28 00:12:35 Daniel: switching to operational runbooks — we'll create a runbook for keys compromise, egress breach, and model rollback. recommended RTO for critical path is 15 minutes with warm spares.
00:12:50 Ravi: that runbook needs to be testable in our DR rehearsals.
00:12:55 Daniel: we can run a tabletop and a live failover during the PoC week.
00:13:03 Maya: note: we'll schedule PoC capacity testing the week of Dec 8 as discussed.
00:13:08 Lena: latency for cert rotation—how disruptive is a KMS rotation?
00:13:13 Daniel: envelope key rotation is non-disruptive; root key rotation for HSM is scheduled maintenance but we can orchestrate staggered rotation to avoid complete outage.
00:13:24 Omar: are there any endpoints that require internet egress for license checks or telemetry?
00:13:30 Alicia: no license phone-home required for Private; optional telemetry can be turned off.
00:13:36 00:13:50 Ravi: about connectivity — we want mutual TLS to the private registry. do you support private registry via ECR with VPC endpoints?
00:13:58 Daniel: yes, ECR with VPC endpoints is supported, and pull policies can be restricted. image pulls happen from private subnets with no public IPs.
00:14:08 Priya: what's the retention policy for audit logs in hidden storage? can we set retention windows for 7 years?
00:14:15 Daniel: you control the retention on your archival store. we recommend cold storage for long-term retention; Redwood can push to your S3 Glacier or your on-prem archival store.
00:14:27 Lena: any recommendations for penetration testing or attack surface review?
00:14:33 Daniel: we provide a pen-test guide and a list of allowed tests. for Private deployments you can run a full test against your isolated environment. we also run internal red-team exercises.
00:14:45 00:14:58 Omar: can we get an export of all role mappings and active tokens for audit?
00:15:05 Daniel: yes, RBAC exports are available via API and we can produce a snapshot for auditors. tokens are short-lived but we can provide token issuance logs.
00:15:16 Priya: one nuance — our compliance team wants proof that admin API calls are multi-signed for certain actions. do you offer an out-of-band approval workflow?
00:15:26 Daniel: we have an approvals workflow that can require a second approver for destructive ops and can integrate with your ticketing system for dual control.
00:15:38 00:15:55 Alicia: ok, I'm going to take a minute to record the action items and the asks we heard.
00:16:02 Alicia: action: Daniel to draw VPC diagram showing NAT, egress proxy, bastion, and private endpoints; Daniel to include fail-closed vs fail-open patterns.
00:16:15 Alicia: action: Alicia to share SOC 2 pack and pipeline attestation; Alicia to propose dates for PoC and runbook rehearsal.
00:16:25 Alicia: action: Omar to provide egress allowlist and required telemetry endpoints; Priya to list compliance reporting windows.
00:16:36 Ravi: sounds good. can we also get a matrix of data residency controls by component?
00:16:42 Daniel: yes, will include component residency map in the diagram.
00:16:48 00:17:00 Lena: one technical question — how do you handle long-running KV cache state during a worker recycle? is there a warm transfer?
00:17:08 Daniel: KV cache is ephemeral. for long-running sessions we persist session pointers in a small fast cache (in-region) and use sticky routing to keep sessions on the same worker; warm transfer isn't supported for large KV objects today.
00:17:24 Omar: that's acceptable if we can pin sessions and limit worker churn during trading windows.
00:17:31 Daniel: you can configure maintenance windows and disable autoscaling during critical hours.
00:17:40 00:18:05 Ravi: any gotchas with private DNS and split-horizon?
00:18:12 Daniel: ensure your internal resolver can resolve private-hosted zones; we recommend DNS conditional forwarding. also make sure reverse DNS is consistent for IP allow-lists.
00:18:23 Priya: can we get a sample policy for least-privilege roles?
00:18:29 Daniel: we'll include a starter RBAC manifest listing admin, infra, dev, and read-only roles and examples of least-privilege permissions.
00:18:40 Alicia: time check — we're about halfway, do we want to dig into SIEM integration or KMS HSM specifics next?
00:18:48 Ravi: let's do KMS/HSM specifics first.
00:18:53 Daniel: for HSM we support CloudHSM and customer HSM connectors. when using customer HSM, the Redwood process requests a wrapped key via your KMIP endpoint; we never persist wrapping keys.
00:19:05 Omar: do you support KMIP for on-prem HSMs?
00:19:09 Daniel: yes, KMIP is supported; setup requires network connectivity from control plane to the HSM or a proxying appliance in your network.
00:19:18 Priya: how is access to key management audited?
00:19:22 Daniel: KMS request logs include requesting principal, operation type, and key ID; we recommend forwarding these to your SIEM and enabling object-level logging.
00:19:34 Maya: minor transcription artifact: sometimes 'KMIP' is transcribed as 'Kemip' in older notes.
00:19:40 (brief laughter)
00:19:48 00:20:00 Daniel: another detail — encryption at rest for model weights uses envelope encryption, so large model files remain in encrypted blobs in your regional storage. we also support field-level encryption for sensitive model inputs.
00:20:13 Ravi: for drift control we want to disable automatic downloads of newer model versions — can that be locked?
00:20:20 Daniel: yes, auto-update is disabled by default in Private; updates happen only via your provisioning pipeline.
00:20:27 Priya: can you sign off on a statement of compliance that says Redwood won't exfiltrate customer prompts from Private?
00:20:35 Alicia: we will provide a contractual clause and tooling proof points in the pack.
00:20:41 00:20:55 Lena: a question on firewalling — do you recommend NGFW or a standard firewall for outbound filtering?
00:21:01 Daniel: NGFW often gives better application-layer controls and better logging for forensics; if you need simpler management, a layered approach with a firewall + egress proxy works well.
00:21:12 Omar: do you support integration with our logging transport that uses mutual auth and a proxy chain?
00:21:18 Daniel: yes, we can configure a chained proxy and mutual TLS to your log collector.
00:21:26 Ravi: any SLA language around private deployments for latency and uptime?
00:21:33 Alicia: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed latency and uptime. for Private deployments SLA is available as an add-on with dedicated support and runbook commitments.
00:21:45 Priya: we'll need contractual language for incident notification times.
00:21:50 Alicia: noted — we'll include incident response SLAs and escalation matrix.
00:21:57 00:22:10 Daniel: quick note on observability — token-level cost metrics can be forwarded as telemetry and mapped to customer routes, which is helpful for chargebacks. you control retention and where those metrics land.
00:22:25 Lena: does metrics telemetry include prompt content?
00:22:29 Daniel: metrics do not include prompt content, only high-level counts and latencies.
00:22:35 Priya: important for compliance.
00:22:40 00:22:50 Ravi: let's role-play a compromise — assume an operator credential is phished. what's the sequence of events and controls that contain the blast radius?
00:22:59 Daniel: good scenario. controls: short TTLs on tokens, mandatory MFA, JIT console access, and approvals for destructive ops. detection: SIEM triggers on anomalous API calls; response: immediate token revocation, rotate affected keys, and fail-closed egress if suspicious external calls start. we'll provide a runbook with timelines and responsible parties.
00:23:23 Omar: do you provide automation for token revocation across sessions?
00:23:27 Daniel: yes, revoke-by-user API call invalidates tokens and triggers session termination.
00:23:34 Alicia: near the end — let's recap next steps and the PoC plan.
00:23:40 Alicia: recap: we'll deliver SOC 2 pack, VPC diagram, RBAC manifest, and schedule PoC the week of Dec 8. customer to provide egress allowlist and required SIEM endpoints.
00:23:54 Ravi: agreed. can you also provide an estimated cost for dedicated GPU pool vs Private appliance for our expected 250 RPS?
00:24:03 Alicia: yes, I'll include a cost sheet.
00:24:09 Priya: compliance will review the artifact pack and come back with questions.
00:24:14 Alicia: perfect — any final questions?
00:24:18 Lena: none from me.
00:24:20 Omar: no, thanks.
00:24:22 Alicia: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with materials and the PoC calendar.
00:24:28 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: medium — typical ASR artifacts (misspelling of KMIP, KV mentions), occasional overlapping talk, and speaker labels verified manually.
